result.title: DPMA: Learning to Compress Mixture-of-Experts Models
result.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures offer high computational efficiency, but storing all experts requires substantial memory and limits deployment on resource-constrained hardware. Most retraining-free MoE compression methods commit to either pruning or merging experts, often with a uniform compression ratio across layers. We introduce DPMA (Differentiable Prune Merge Absorb), which jointly learns compression operations and layer-wise expert allocation through gradient descent under a global expert budget. Separate learnable coefficients allow DPMA to prune experts, merge their parameters, and absorb their routing contributions by forwarding routing weights to retained experts. These coefficients and expert assignments are optimised to match the original model's outputs on calibration data while its weights remain frozen. Across four MoE models, eight multiple-choice benchmarks, and five compression ratios, DPMA achieves the highest accuracy averaged over benchmarks and compression ratios on each model among the evaluated methods. At $75\%$ expert reduction, it outperforms the strongest baseline on every model, with gains of up to $6.7$ percentage points.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DPMA，在全局专家预算约束下用可学习系数通过梯度下降联合决定剪枝、参数合并与路由吸收三种操作，并学习逐层专家分配；原权重冻结，仅以校准数据的输出对齐来优化系数与分配。
AI.relevance_reason: 「全局预算 + 可微的逐层容量分配与操作选择」可供核查是否能借鉴到 LVR 中每层或每步 latent 计算的预算分配与操作决策，但本文属 MoE 压缩、与视觉推理无直接联系，迁移仅属推测。
